utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon everyone. The court is in session. Registrar, could you kindly call the case of the current hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon. This is case number IT-98-32/1-A, The Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Milan Lukic, can you hear and follow the proceedings in a language which you understand? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can hear it in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, can you hear and follow the proceedings in a language which you understand? THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have the appearances, please. Starting by the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. My name is Virginie Monchy. I represent the OTP today. With me is Mr. Paul Rogers who is the senior appeals counsel, as well as Mrs. Lourdes Galicia who is our Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Turning now to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Tomislav Visnjic for the Defence of Milan Lukic, together with Mr. Dragan Ivetic, Vladimir Bozovic, and Dalida Chrysostomidou.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Djuro Cepic, Jens Dieckmann, and Sabine Schulz for the Defence of Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This Status Conference was convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis B and C of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal which requires that a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days after the last status conference. The main purpose of a Status Conference is to give any detainee pending an appeals ruling the possibility to raise issues in relation thereto including its mental -- his or her mental physical condition of the accused. First Status Conference hearing was held on the 13th of November, 2009, we are therefore meeting today for the second Status Conference. At this juncture, I'd like to highlight the developments which have taken place from the point of view of procedure since we last met. First I'd like to recall that the Trial Chamber rendered its judgement in this case on the 20th of July 2009. The Office of the Prosecutor filed its notice of appeal on the 19th of August, 2009, against Sredoje Lukic. The Defence of Milan Lukic as well as the Defence of Sredoje Lukic have both filed their notice of appeals on the 19th of August, 2009. The Office of the Prosecutor filed the public version of its appeals brief against Sredoje Lukic on the 2nd of November, 2009. The Defence of Sredoje Lukic filed its respondent brief on the 14th of December, 2009, and the Prosecutor filed its brief in reply on the 23rd of December, 2009. The Defence of Sredoje Lukic has also filed its appeals brief with a redacted public version and a confidential version on the 2nd of November, 2009. The Prosecutor filed his respondent brief on the 14th of December, 2009, and Sredoje Lukic filed his brief in reply on the 29th of December, 2009. The Defence of Milan Lukic filed his appeals brief on the 17th of December, 2009, pursuant to the decision issued by the Appeals Chamber on the 30th of October, 2009, which granted him an extension of the time. The Prosecutor filed the -- his respondent brief on the 5th of February, 2010. And Milan Lukic filed his brief in reply on the 22nd of February, 2010. I should like to thank the parties for having met the dead-lines of submissions so as to ensure smooth running of the proceedings. Furthermore, I should like to mention that the Appeals Chamber is now seised of three confidential motions written by the Defence, and dated respectively 8th of February, 2010; 10th of February, 2010; and 22nd of February, 2010, in which it is asked to consider granting Milan Lukic the possibility to introduce additional evidence. And I would like to inform the parties that the Appeals Chamber will issue its decisions in due course, and that will take place before the hearing. Later on, the Appeals Chamber will set the date of the appeals hearing. It is now too early to set the official time of the appeals hearing. What is likely is that the appeals hearing will not be held before June 2010. I would now like to turn to the issue of detentions, conditions, and the state of the health of Mr. Milan and Sredoje Lukic. Would you like to mention any concerns regarding your conditions of detention or your state of health. Mr. Milan Lukic? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] As far as my health is concerned, it's fine. As far as the detention conditions are concerned, well, when an innocent man is in detention, you know how it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic? THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like to ask the parties whether at this juncture they have any issues that they would like to deal with during this Status Conference. Let me first ask the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have two items we would like to deal with quickly. First in regards of the filing of the public version and the redacted version of our response brief to Mr. Milan Lukic's appeals brief, we have not filed it yet because Milan Lukic has not filed its public redacted version of his own appeals brief. This being said, the Defence of Milan Lukic has told us before the hearing that they were about to file this public redacted version, so we'll be able to file our own respondent brief, our own brief public and redacted. Second item, the date of the hearing and possible questions of the Chamber, the Appeals Chamber, we thank the Appeals Chamber for having told us that the hearing would not be held before June 2010. It this being said, and if this is possible, of course, we would like all parties to be notified at least six weeks in advance of the questions put by the Appeals Chamber as well as the date of the hearing in order to get prepared and to get organised in an efficient manner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Monchy. Now could the Defence of Sredoje Lukic and Milan Lukic tell us what they have to say in response to the items mentioned by the OTP. These two items.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. With regard to the first item, we are prepared to file a public version of our appellant's brief in 24 hours, within 24 hours and a public version of the reply in three or five days, so that would probably be by Monday. That would make it possible for the Prosecution to plan to file their response at more or less the same time. As far as the dead-lines for the appellate hearing is concerned, I would like to draw the Appeals Chamber attention to the fact that we have not yet received a translation of the judgement, a translation into a language that the accused understand. And, therefore, I would request that you grant us at least 30 days from the day the judgement is translated so that we can consult with my client, Milan Lukic, to see if he has any additional requests that concern the appeal and the allegations in the appeal. We have worked with him on this basis, but we believe that an official translation will make it possible for him to fully understand the allegations made in the judgement. Thank you, that would be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I take due note of the comments made by the parties on the first issue. And you will shortly get a written answer on this. As far as the translation of the judgement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the translation of parts of the judgement in a language that the accused can understand, let me tell you that we also took due note of the request and will do everything possible by contacting the linguistic department to make sure that the translation is done swiftly. It will be the translation of the relevant parts of the judgement mainly. As to the date of the appeals hearing, the Trial Chamber -- the Appeals Chamber will do its utmost to accommodate both parties. But let me repeat that at this juncture, all I can say is that the appeals hearing will not be held before June 2010. Do the representative of Mr. Milan Lukic's Defence have anything else to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, what about the counsel of Defence for Mr. Sredoje Lukic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, we can have nothing to raise now, just to say for the transcript our position is that we could join to proposal of our learned friends from OTP related to the issue of notification of commencement of oral hearing six week before the commencement of that hearing. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We take due note of this, and we will try to accommodate your wishes as far as dead-lines -- as far as notice is concerned. As far as I'm concerned, I have no other issues on the agenda. We can thus adjourn for the day, and I would like to thank the parties for their participation, and I also would like to thank all the staff for helping us. This hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
